_note: Typology SVGs named by reading the drawings — the files carry no text metadata. Sets A/B/C are export batches, not categories; many B files duplicate A.
_set_logic:
"A, B and C are export batches, not clean typology categories - the boundaries fall mid-family and should not be used as catalogue groupings.

By actual content there are FOUR families:

1. SLIDING / LIFT-AND-SLIDE (13 unique drawings, 26 files) - straddles A and B. Rendered as shaded grey aluminium elevations with black glass and directional arrows on each operable leaf; several sit in a hatched wall/shutter-box context panel. Covers 1 to 6 sashes, bypass and centre-meeting-stile configurations, a 90/270-degree corner unit, and optional fly screens, louvred shutters and roller shutters. Occupies ALL of folder A (20 files) plus B/Asset 100-105 (6 files) - i.e. the batch spilled over the folder boundary when the second export ran.

2. DIN OPENING SYMBOLS for doors and vents (6 unique, 12 files) - B/Asset 106-117. Completely different visual language: flat EN 12519 / DIN 1356 symbol tiles on a 3x3 divided frame, solid triangles for opening-toward-viewer and dotted triangles for opening-away. Hinged inward/outward doors, parallel-opening, projected/top-hung, and tilt-and-turn.

3. PIVOT CASEMENTS (2 unique, 2 files) - B/Asset 118-119. Portrait 3D-style frames with white pivot-bearing blocks and dashed fold diamonds; vertical axis and horizontal axis.

4. TILT-AND-TURN CASEMENTS (7 unique, 13 files) - all of folder C. Shaded aluminium elevations with hairline diagonal opening marks in the glass. Single and two-light units, side-hung and bottom-hung companions, fixed lights, fanlights/transoms, and P.W.D. (accessible low-threshold) frame variants flagged with a wheelchair pictogram.

The A/B split is therefore an artefact: family 1 was exported twice, the first copy filling folder A and the overflow of the second copy landing at the head of folder B. C is the only folder that maps cleanly onto one family."
